entry.title: Installing Git Bash on Windows: A Beginner’s Guide
entry.summary:
What You’ll Learn in This Part
Introduction What Is Git Bash Installing Git Bash (Windows Edition) Conclusion GitHub and Git Bash are tools used to create, manage, and collaborate on digital projects—especially projects that involve code, data, or files that change over time. These tools are widely used by software developers, data analysts, data scientists, programmers, students and even non-programmers. Anyone who wants a reliable way to track their work, avoid losing progress, and collaborate with others can benefit from using Git Bash and GitHub. Git Bash is a tool you use on your computer to communicate with Git, the version control system that tracks changes in your files. It provides a simple terminal where you can: Navigate folders Create files Record changes using clear, text-based commands. GitHub, on the other hand, is an online platform where those recorded changes are stored, shared, and displayed. When you use Git Bash, you save your work locally as commits and then send them to GitHub, where your projects are safely stored online and can be accessed from anywhere. In simple terms, Git Bash acts as the bridge between your computer and Git, while GitHub serves as the online home for your projects. Together, they help one track progress, collaborate confidently, and build a clear, visible history of their work. Install Git on your PC. You can download it here.

entry.summary: Abstract Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) has established itself as a popular approach for defining requirements and validating software, mainly due to its promise of aligning business, development, and testing through a simple, behavior-oriented language. However, the large-scale adoption of BDD, especially in complex corporate environments, has highlighted practical limitations related to semantic ambiguity, maintainability, and misuse as a mere automation layer. This article introduces RCt2 (Rich Case Test – Tier 2) as an evolutionary and pragmatic proposal. entry.title: Nous Research's NousCoder-14B is an open-source coding model landing right in the Claude Code moment
entry.summary: Nous Research, the open-source artificial intelligence startup backed by crypto venture firm Paradigm, released a new competitive programming model on Monday that it says matches or exceeds several larger proprietary systems — trained in just four days using 48 of Nvidia's latest B200 graphics processors. The model, called NousCoder-14B, is another entry in a crowded field of AI coding assistants, but arrives at a particularly charged moment: Claude Code, the agentic programming tool from rival Anthropic, has dominated social media discussion since New Year's Day, with developers posting breathless testimonials about its capabilities. The simultaneous developments underscore how quickly AI-assisted software development is evolving — and how fiercely companies large and small are competing …

entry.title: The creator of Claude Code just revealed his workflow, and developers are losing their minds
entry.summary:
When the creator of the world's most advanced coding agent speaks, Silicon Valley doesn't just listen — it takes notes. For the past week, the engineering community has been dissecting a thread on X from Boris Cherny, the creator and head of Claude Code at Anthropic. What began as a casual sharing of his personal terminal setup has spiraled into a viral manifesto on the future of software development, with industry insiders calling it a watershed moment for the startup.
"If you're not reading the Claude Code best practices straight from its creator, you're behind as a programmer," wrote Jeff Tang, a prominent voice in the developer community.
